newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed, market consolidating.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed, market consolidating.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed as the market consolidated following limit gains Tuesday in response to the USDA's August crop production estimate, traders said.
"It's just trying to get its bearings right now, looking for direction," a trader said.
Futures were underpinned by Merrill Lynch Futures purchase of six million bushels of December and purchase of nine million bushels of July, traders said.

The market was pressured by Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report but it remained underpinned by Tuesday's surprisingly low corn production forecast for the 1997 U.S. crop by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of old crop corn during the week ended August 7 totalled a minus 23,800 tonnes, below expectations for 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes. Net export sales of new crop corn totalled 160,100 tonnes, below expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Corn futures closed two cents per bushel higher to two lower, with September up two cents at $2.64-1/4 a bushel. December was up 1-1/2 at $2.68.

Weather was also viewed as bearish. The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook Wednesday was for below normal temperatures and normal to above normal precipitation in the U.S. Midwest from August 19 to August 23.
But hesitant selling interest lingered amid USDA's Tuesday forecast for 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.276 billion bushels, below an average of analysts' estimates for 9.554 billion bushels.
Cargill Inc sold five million bushels of December and Refco Inc sold six million December but also bought two million bushels of December, traders said.

In spread dealings, Cargill Inc did two million bushels of September/December at four to 4-1/4 cents, premium December and Continental Grain did two million bushels of March/July at seven cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 72,000 contracts, below the 121,667 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 2,000 December $2.50 puts at 5-1/2 cents and Prudential Securities bought 500 September $2.60 calls at 4-1/2 to six cents, traders said. Continental Grain bought 500 December $2.60 puts at 10 cents and sold 500 Dec $3.00 calls at five cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 41,817 traded Wednesday.
